technical__0.tagline: Hunt the bug. Beat the clock.
rules: Each team will be given a buggy code snippet in a language of their choice (C, C++, Python, or Java).
Participants must identify and fix all bugs within the given time limit.
Use of the internet, AI tools, or external references is strictly prohibited.
Code must compile and produce the correct expected output to be considered valid.
Partial fixes will receive partial marks based on the judge's evaluation.
Teams found using unfair means will be disqualified immediately.
The decision of the judges is final and binding.
Teams must design and develop a webpage based on the theme revealed at the start of the event.
Only HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript are allowed. No frameworks or libraries.
All assets (images, fonts, icons) must be either self-created or royalty-free.
Internet access is permitted only for downloading assets, not for copying code.
The final submission must be a working, self-contained HTML file.
Judging criteria: creativity (40%), functionality (30%), responsiveness (30%).
Plagiarism or use of templates will result in immediate disqualification.

technical__2.tagline: Pitch your idea. Win the sharks.
rules: Each team must present an original business or tech idea to a panel of judges.
Presentation time is strictly 5 minutes; a warning bell rings at 4:30.
A 3-minute Q&A session follows every pitch — be prepared for tough questions.
Slides are optional but must be submitted 30 minutes before the event starts.
Ideas must be original and not previously funded or launched as a real business.
Judging criteria: innovation (30%), feasibility (25%), market potential (25%), presentation (20%).
Props, demos, or prototypes are encouraged and will earn bonus consideration.

technical__3.tagline: Build it. Show it. Inspire them.
rules: Teams must display a working project (hardware, software, or hybrid) at their assigned booth.
Projects must have been built by the team members themselves; pre-made kits are not allowed.
A working demo must be available throughout the exhibition for judges and attendees.
A 2-minute verbal explanation of the project is required when judges visit.
All necessary equipment, power banks, and materials must be brought by the team.
Judging criteria: innovation (35%), functionality (30%), presentation (20%), impact (15%).
Teams must be present at their stall at all times during judging hours.
Teams will receive an initial clue and must solve a series of technical puzzles to find subsequent clues.
Clues are spread across the college campus; teams must not damage or move any clue markers.
Mobile phones may be used for calculations only — browsing, calling, or messaging is prohibited.
Each team gets one lifeline: a 60-second hint from the organizer, usable only once.
The team that reaches the final location first with all correct answers wins.
Running inside the college building is not permitted.
Any team found tampering with another team's clues will be disqualified.

technical__5.tagline: Prompt it. Generate it. Amaze them.
rules: Participants must create a short video (30–90 seconds) using any AI video generation tool.
The video must be based on the theme announced at the start of the event.
Allowed tools: Sora, Runway, Pika, Kling, or any other publicly available AI video generator.
Participants must submit both the final video and the prompts used to create it.
Videos must be original; pre-generated or pre-downloaded videos are not allowed.
Judging criteria: creativity (40%), theme relevance (30%), video quality (30%).
Explicit, offensive, or copyrighted content will lead to immediate disqualification.
The quiz consists of 30 multiple-choice questions covering logical reasoning, quantitative aptitude, and verbal ability.
Each correct answer awards 1 mark; there is no negative marking.
Participants must use only the provided answer sheet; rough work on any other paper is not allowed.
Use of mobile phones, calculators, or any electronic device is strictly prohibited.
Once the answer sheet is submitted, no changes can be made.
In case of a tie, a rapid-fire sudden death round will be conducted.
The quiz will begin exactly at the scheduled time; latecomers will not be given extra time.

nontechnical__0.tagline: Drop in. Be the last squad standing.
rules: Each squad must consist of exactly 4 players registered under a single team name.
Players must use their own mobile devices; emulators are strictly not allowed.
The match mode will be Classic Squad on a map decided by the organizers.
Cheating, hacking, or use of mods will result in permanent disqualification of the entire squad.
All players must be present at the venue at least 15 minutes before match time.
Points are calculated based on kills and final placement using the official BGMI tournament scoring system.
The organizer's decision regarding any dispute is final.

nontechnical__1.tagline: Every move matters. Outthink your opponent.
rules: The tournament follows standard FIDE chess rules.
Time control is Rapid: 10 minutes per player with no increment.
A player who runs out of time loses the game, regardless of board position.
Touching a piece obligates the player to move it if a legal move exists (touch-move rule).
Mobile phones must be switched off or kept face-down during the match.
Matches are played in a Swiss-system format; the top players advance to knockout rounds.
Disputes must be raised immediately and will be settled by the designated arbiter.
Each pair consists of one artist and one model; both must be registered participants.
Only face-safe, water-based, non-toxic paints are allowed. Bring your own supplies.
The design theme will be revealed 5 minutes before the event starts.
Participants must stop painting immediately when time is called.
Glitter, gems, and accessories may be used as additions but must be safe for skin.
Judging criteria: creativity (40%), theme relevance (35%), neatness (25%).
Pre-drawn stencils or pre-painted models are not allowed.
Competition is conducted in a single-elimination knockout format.
Participants are categorized by gender; mixed-gender matches are at the participant's discretion.
Both players must grip the handle with the elbow on the pad; the referee sets the starting position.
The match begins only after the referee gives the 'Go' signal.
A point is won when the opponent's hand is pinned to the pad. Best of 3 points wins the match.
Lifting the elbow off the pad, slipping the grip, or using the shoulder illegally results in a foul.
Two fouls in a match result in a forfeit of that match.

nontechnical__4.tagline: Recreate the pixel. Spot the image.
rules: Teams will be shown a pixelated or partially revealed image and must identify or recreate it.
There are multiple rounds: identification round and a recreation round on grid paper.
Internet access, mobile phones, and reference materials are not allowed.
Teams must write their answers clearly on the provided answer sheet.
Judging in the recreation round is based on accuracy and completeness.
Teams have a maximum of 3 skip attempts across all rounds combined.
The team with the highest cumulative score across all rounds wins.

nontechnical__5.tagline: A pencil, a blank page, your imagination.
rules: The topic or subject for sketching will be announced at the start of the event.
Only pencils, charcoal, and erasers are allowed. Pens, markers, or colours are not permitted.
Participants must bring their own art supplies; A3 sketch paper will be provided.
Tracing, stenciling, or use of reference images is not allowed.
Participants must stop drawing immediately when time is called by the invigilator.
Judging criteria: creativity (35%), technique (30%), theme relevance (20%), composition (15%).
Sketches must remain anonymous during judging; do not write your name on the front of the sheet.
